sections.title: DISCUSSION
sections.text:
Issued at 129 AM EDT Sat Sep 26 2026

In the upper levels, a ridge is over the Mississippi Valley and a 
closed low is just off the coast of the Mid-Atlantic. At the 
surface, high pressure is centered over the Great Lakes extending 
southward to the Gulf Coast. A Nor'easter is just off the coast of 
the Mid-Atlantic. Dry, sunny weather with pleasant temperatures will 
continue this weekend and into early next week with highs mainly in 
the 70s.  

By midweek, the pattern starts to change with a weak ridge over the 
Southeast and a closed low developing over the Southwest. A warming 
trend will become noticeable by Tuesday or Wednesday with highs in 
the 80s for the rest of the workweek. Some low rain chances are in 
the forecast for Thursday and Friday to account for uncertainty but 
it looks like the system will move northeast into the Midwest late 
in the workweek.

enso.title: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory
paragraphs: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory Synopsis: El Niño is strengthening, with a greater than 90% chance of a very strong event during the Northern Hemisphere fall and winter 2026-27. El Niño strengthened further over the past month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +3.0°C in the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Except for the Niño-4 index, which decreased to +0.1°C in August, values in the other Niño indices increased, reaching +1.8°C in Niño-3.4, +2.5°C in Niño-3, and +3.4°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) remained steady during August [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline [Fig. 4] . Subsurface temperatures continued to be significantly above average, with widespread anomalies in excess of +10.0°C at depth. Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies extended from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices remained negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6

-8] . During the October-December 2026 season, there is a 75% chance of a historic event that would exceed the strength of previous El Niño events dating back to 1950 (+2.5°C or more for a 3-month RONI value ). With an event of this magnitude, the chances of experiencing impacts consistent with El Niño are larger, though not guaranteed (see CPC outlooks for probabilities of seasonal anomalies). In summary, El Niño is strengthening, with a greater than 90% chance of a very strong event during the Northern Hemisphere fall and winter 2026-27. This discussion is a consolidated effort of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), NOAA's National Weather Service, and their funded institutions. Oceanic and atmospheric conditions are updated weekly on the Climate Prediction Center web site (

md.areas: parts of western Kansas and northwestern Oklahoma
md.summary: Increasing thunderstorm development may slowly strengthen and become better organized while spreading northeastward through 4-6 PM CDT. The associated risk for severe wind and hail appears mostly marginal in nature and it still appears unlikely that a severe weather watch will be needed. However, trends will continue to be monitored.
md.discussion: A couple of weak/low-amplitude short wave perturbations are progressing through modest southwesterly flow across the Texas South Plains through central Great Plains early this afternoon. This is occurring on the western periphery of fairly prominent mid-level ridging centered (in the 700-500 mb layer) across the southeastern Great Plains. In the wake of the lead perturbation, and in advance of the trailing one, latest objective analysis indicates that a corridor of stronger boundary-layer destabilization is underway near the western Oklahoma/Texas border vicinity through southwestern Kansas. This is occurring in response to low-level moistening and insolation along the weaker southwestern periphery of expansive cool surface ridging (centered over Quebec), and forecast to slowly shift north-northeastward through 21-23Z. As it does, Rapid Refresh output suggests that mixed-layer CAPE may continue increase through the 1000-2000 J/kg range, and the environment may gradually become more conducive to organizing thunderstorm development in the presence of modest shear. Beneath mid-level flow on the order of 30 kt, this could perhaps include evolving supercell structures and an upscale growing cluster. However, rather modest lower/mid-tropospheric lapse rates and temperature/dew point spreads seem likely to result in mostly marginal severe wind and hail potential.
